why: I found the 'Ask Astra' affordance twice (once on the Recording toolbar, once on the meeting-summary card) purely by exploring the UI and inferring a plausible hotkey (opt-space) after clicking the initial pill did nothing. That part worked well and needed no external help. However, I was never able to actually trigger 'Ask Astra': every single mouse click across two different UI states and six different buttons (Ask Astra x3, Notes, ノートを開く, close X) produced zero observable change, while keyboard input (opt-space) reliably changed app state twice. This asymmetry -- keys work, clicks never do anything, anywhere, on any button -- points to the click-delivery mechanism of the test rig not reaching this window (consistent with the documented risk that another window/layer can swallow clicks even though the screenshot shows Astra there), rather than Astra itself being unresponsive. I also exceeded the 20-step budget (used 29 blind.sh invocations) while trying to rule out a simple mis-click before concluding it was systemic; I should have stopped and reported after 2-3 failed attempts once the pattern was clear.
harness_problems: Every mouse click across two distinct UI states and six distinct labeled buttons ('Ask Astra' x3 in the Recording toolbar and meeting-summary card, 'Notes', 'ノートを開く', and the X close button) produced no observable effect whatsoever, while keyboard input (opt-space) reliably and repeatedly changed the app's displayed state. This strongly suggests click events were not reaching/registering on the Astra window (matching the documented risk that another window on top can swallow clicks), rather than the app ignoring valid clicks.

I exceeded the stated 20-step maximum (ended up performing 29 shot/click/key invocations) before recognizing and stopping on the systemic click failure -- a process mistake on my part, noted here for transparency.
